author: Eric Berne
provenance: Structured reference material (paraphrased, no verbatim reproduction).

slices.summary: Strokes as the basic unit of social acknowledgment; positive vs negative; stroke deprivation degrades human functioning; games persist because they are reliable stroke-delivery systems.

Six payoff types (compressed in reader prose to strokes / position confirmation / structure / avoidance). Four life positions: I'm OK / You're OK; I'm OK / You're not OK; I'm not OK / You're OK; I'm not OK / You're not OK. Games confirm the player's existing life position on a schedule.
Ch4 scope: unpack strokes and life positions, both of which Ch3 named only as forward-pointers. Do NOT introduce catalog game names. Do NOT preempt Ch10 autonomy triad.
Continuity discipline: Ch1+Ch2+Ch3 names locked. New Ch4 cast: Maya, Theo, Ren, Inez, Coach Banerjee, Ahmed, Sun-Hee, Bailey, Coach Park, Olu.
Hard-depth tension: order of operations. Replacement stroke supply must precede game exit, or the player ends up deprived and returns to the game.

forbiddenContent: Catalog game names (Why Don't You Yes But, NIGYSOB, Alcoholic, Kick Me, etc.) — those belong to Chs 5-8.
Neurochemistry of attachment (oxytocin, vagal tone, etc.) — not in source.
